newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - July 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - July 15.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.

- Kwon Young-hae, director of the Agency for National Security Planning, said the agency is considering allowing South Korea's allies to interview Hwang Jang-yop, the highest ranking North Korean ever to defect to South Korea.

- The U.S. defence ministry said it will open a temporary liason office in Pyongyang from July 16 to September 11 in order to carry out a mission to find the remains of U.S. soldiers who died during the 1950-52 Korean War.

- The number of registered vehicles in Korea is expected to surpass the 10 million mark on Tuesday, the Ministry of Construction and Transportation said. The ministry said it would impose tolls to enter and exit downtown areas of South Korea's six major cities.

- The presidential nomination race of the ruling New Korea Party was heading for a furore on Monday, as Park Chan-jong, one of the seven contenders, made an explosive allegation that his main rival, ex-chairman Lee Hoi-chang, was buying votes.
